On a lieu de soupçonner que la fermentation s’est emparée des récoltes engrangées ou mises en meules, lorsqu’on s’aperçoit qu’elles émettent une chaleur qui n’est pas ordinaire : il faut alors immédiatement les dégranger ou les ôter de meule, afin de les étendre à l’air ; mais cette opération même demande à être conduite avec prudence, et il faut enlever couche par couche ; car il n’est d’observation que lorsque le foin, la paille, etc., sont en fermentation, il suffit quelquefois de les étendre brusquement ou d’y faire un trou, pour que l’incendie éclate sur-le-champ.

glosses: A granary; a store of grain.

examples.text: That our garners may be full, affording all manner of store: that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets.
Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.

glosses: An accumulation, supply, store, or hoard of something.

examples.text:
Master, I bring from many wanderings,
The gathered garner of my years to thee;
One precious fruit of many rain-blown springs
And sun-shod summers, ripened over-sea.

glosses: To reap grain, gather it up, and store it in a granary.

examples.text: The rustic does not know what would happen to him if he garnered his corn on Sunday, nor does the diner-out in polite society know what would happen if he spooned up his food with his knife - but they both are stricken with a sort of paralysis at the very suggestion of infringing these taboos.

glosses: To gather, amass, hoard, as if harvesting grain.

examples.text: […] I walked enormous distances[…] garnering thoughts even from the heather.
He garnered the fruit of his studies in seven volumes.
[…] its fleet went out to garner in the elusive but highly succulent fish.

glosses: To earn; to get; to accumulate or acquire by some effort or due to some fact

examples.text: to garner support
He garnered a reputation as a language expert.
Her new book garnered high praise from the critics.
His poor choices garnered him a steady stream of welfare checks.
This country will never forget nor fail to honor those who have so courageously garnered our highest regard.
President Roosevelt garnered the support of our working men and women to increase war production and build our "Arsenal of Democracy."
The AMPTP has disputed that description as a “mischaracterization” of their proposal meant to “garner support for its work stoppage.”

glosses: To gather or become gathered; to accumulate or become accumulated; to become stored.

examples.text: She soothed herself with the belief that the workings of her soul were still known to him,—that her regret and her despondency were but the needful preparation for that other sphere, where now her only remaining hope was garnered.
For this alone on Death I wreak / The wrath that garners in my heart;
